title: Simultaneous characterization of porous and non-porous electrodes in microbial electrochemical systems
author: Prado, Berenguer, et al.
materials: Chronoamperometry is one of the most important characterization techniques of microbial electrochemical systems, so it was used to validate our simultaneous multielectrode analysis. Three different porous carbonaceous materials were used as working electrodes (WE) in a single chamber cell. These materials differed in electrical conductivity (WE1, WE2 and WE3, from lowest to highest electrical conductivity). The wiring was done as described in section one (Fig. 3C-c.2). The counter electrode and reference electrode were identical to those described in section one. The cell had a volume of 500 mL, the electrolyte used was Fresh Water Medium (FWM). FWM contained the following mineral salts (per liter): 2.2 g of Na2HPO4, 1.18 g of NaH2PO4, 0.64 g of NH4Cl, 0.26 g of KCl and 0.024 g of C6H5FeO7 (ferric citrate). Moreover, it includes a mix of vitamins and trace minerals [10]. Acetate (20 mM) was supplied as the sole carbon and electron donor. Anaerobic conditions were achieved by flushing the culture media with N2 to remove oxygen and a phosphate buffer was used to keep a pH of 7. This medium was inoculated with 20 mL of Geobacter sulfurreducens pure culture with an OD600 = 0.6.

Fig. 4A shows the calculated values of current produced by each of the three working electrodes, the bigger electrical current value corresponds to the electrode material with lower electrical resistance. These values were calculated through the instantaneous potential difference measured in each working electrode and the value of the resistor used in the external circuit (1 KΩ). The total sum of the currents produced by each working electrode measured by the aid of the Keithley multimeter (blue line in Fig. 4A) was the same as the one recorded by the NEV-4 potentiostat (see fitting in Fig. 4B). Furthermore, the real potential ​​of each working electrode remained constant around 0.23 V over time for the different electrodes (Fig. 4A). The difference of 30 mV between the set and measured potentials is assigned to the inevitable circuit and connections resistances, but this small value supports that the electrochemical characterization based on the proposed method has been carried out successfully.Fig. 4(A) Current intensity and polarization potential associated to the 3 working electrodes of the MEC including the summation of all currents. (B) Comparison of the total current recorded by both the multimeter and the potentiostat.Fig 4

steps.title: Prepare anaerobic growth medium
steps.instruction: Make 500 mL of Fresh Water Medium (FWM) containing per liter: 2.2 g Na2HPO4, 1.18 g NaH2PO4, 0.64 g NH4Cl, 0.26 g KCl, 0.024 g ferric citrate (C6H5FeO7), plus the required vitamins and trace minerals. Add acetate to a final concentration of 20 mM as the sole carbon/electron donor. Adjust the pH to 7 with the phosphate buffer. Flush the medium with N2 (or N2:CO2 if a bicarbonate buffer is used) to remove dissolved oxygen and keep it under continuous magnetic stirring (laminar agitation preferred). Inoculate with 20 mL of a Geobacter sulfurreducens pure culture at OD600 = 0.6.

substeps.instruction: Weigh and dissolve the listed salts in deionized water.
Add the vitamin and trace‑mineral mix.
Introduce acetate to reach 20 mM.
Adjust pH to 7 with phosphate buffer.
Deoxygenate by N2 (or N2:CO2) flushing.
Stir continuously with a magnetic stirrer.
Inoculate with the specified culture volume.

steps.title: Assemble MEC cell and electrodes
steps.instruction: Place three porous carbonaceous working electrodes (WE1, WE2, WE3) of differing conductivity, one counter electrode, and an Ag/AgCl (sat.) reference electrode into a single‑chamber cell of 500 mL volume. Ensure all electrodes are fully immersed in the deoxygenated medium. Include a blank electrode with a known response for validation.

substeps.instruction: Insert the three working electrodes into the chamber.
Add the counter electrode and the reference electrode.
Verify complete immersion of all electrodes.
Add the optional blank electrode.

steps.title: Wire electrodes with corrosion‑resistant junctions
steps.instruction: Create corrosion‑resistant wire‑material connections for each working electrode. First promote electrical contact by inserting the wire into a drilled hole, tying it, or using conductive adhesive/tape or an intermediate conductive material. Then protect the junction by coating it with a non‑corroding resin‑like adhesive. Attach a 1 kΩ shunt resistor in series with each working electrode (or select a resistor value appropriate for the expected current).

substeps.instruction: Prepare the wire length needed for each electrode.
Promote contact: insert wire, tie, or apply conductive adhesive.
Apply a resin‑like protective coating over the junction.
Solder or clamp a 1 kΩ shunt resistor in series with the electrode.

steps.title: Connect electrodes to potentiostat and multimeter
steps.instruction: Join all working‑electrode wires together and connect them to the working terminal of a Nanoelectra NEV‑4 single‑channel potentiostat. Connect the reference electrode to the RE pin and the counter electrode to the CE pin of the potentiostat. Link each shunt resistor to a current‑measuring channel of a Keithley 2700 multichannel multimeter, and also connect a potential‑measuring channel between each working electrode and the reference electrode. Optionally, place an additional current channel in series with the counter electrode to verify total current.

substeps.instruction: Wire the three working electrodes to the potentiostat working terminal.
Connect the Ag/AgCl reference electrode to the RE input.
Connect the counter electrode to the CE input.
Attach each shunt resistor to a Keithley current channel.
Connect a Keithley potential channel between each WE and RE.
Optionally, insert a current channel in series with the counter electrode.

steps.title: Set potentiostat potential and start recording
steps.instruction: Program the Nanoelectra NEV‑4 potentiostat to polarize each working electrode at +0.2 V versus Ag/AgCl (sat.). Begin chronoamperometric acquisition to log the overall current. Simultaneously start data logging on the Keithley multimeter to capture the voltage across each shunt resistor (for current) and the WE‑RE potential.

steps.title: Monitor individual currents and verify totals
steps.instruction: Continuously observe the recorded potentials (expected ~0.23 V, within ~30 mV of the set value) and calculate each individual current using I = V_shunt / 1 kΩ. Confirm that the sum of the three individual currents equals both the current measured at the counter electrode and the total current reported by the potentiostat.

substeps.instruction: Convert each shunt‑resistor voltage to current.
Check that each WE‑RE potential stays around 0.23 V.
Add the three individual currents and compare to the counter‑electrode current and potentiostat total.

steps.title: Validate wiring via abiotic cyclic voltammetry
steps.instruction: Optionally, perform cyclic voltammetry on the assembled cell without microbial inoculation to ensure that no corrosion‑derived currents are present, confirming the effectiveness of the protective wiring strategy.
